newsitem.title: USA: San Franciscans oppose paying for stadium - poll.
newsitem.headline: San Franciscans oppose paying for stadium - poll.

text.p: San Francisco voters would reject spending tax funds on a new football park stadium the National Football League's 49ers, according to a poll published on Monday.

Despite the team's popularity, only 28 percent of city voters would say "yes" to building a new stadium financed "in part by public funds," according to a poll by the San Francisco Chronicle newspaper.
Sixty-five percent of those surveyed said they would oppose using public funds, the poll found.
Only seven percent of those polled said they were undecided, the Chronicle said.
The San Francisco 49ers, which have sought out of aging Candlestick Park for years, recently proposed a new 74,000-seat stadium expected to cost about $250 million.
Officials with the team said they wanted to develop a public-private partnership to finance the facility.
The Chronicle said its survey of 600 registered San Francisco voters was conducted Oct 12 to Oct 15.
